invariants.I94POOL: For owner-led split, snapshot baseline B=parent.counts and available pool R=parent.limits-B, componentwise over exactly implementation, initial_review, remediation, final_review, design_reset. One atomic split event allocates all selected children. Each allocation A is a complete nonnegative bounded-integer map with at least one positive component; sum(A) must be <=R in every component. Child effective counts initialize to B; limits initialize to B+A, without adding COUNTS defaults. Each local counted start increments both local and effective counts exactly once. Nested splits allocate only that child's remaining effective allowance. Unallocated remainder is permanently unavailable after retirement; no subsequent allocation, transfer or reopening event is accepted. Historical consumption is reported once at its origin, never summed repeatedly as sibling consumption. Explicit distinct grants retain their existing policy meaning; splits themselves grant no attempts.
invariants.I94SPLIT: Owner-led split uses strict data fields authority, capsule, children, reason. authority is named user authority; capsule is the exact current parent reference; children is a nonempty list of strict objects issue, counts, capsule, where capsule is that child's complete generation-one capsule. Issue IDs are positive, unique, different from the parent, and unique as allocation targets across repository histories. The child capsule must match repository and child issue and pass existing complete-capsule and pinned-owner validation. Require parent ready, no active or suspended phase, no unresolved blocker, no failed final review, no pending repair, no failed-verification repair requirement and no unresolved failed initial review or consequential challenge. A passed subsequent final review may resolve initial-review failure for this purpose. Delivered or already retired parents cannot split. Retirement and all allocations occur in the one event. Keep the existing timed split event shape and replay behavior unchanged.
invariants.I94LOCAL: A native owner-led child uses existing initialize fields, policy owner-led-v1, adoption null and predecessor {issue,digest}. The digest identifies the exact parent prefix ending with its owner-led split. The parent must exist, have the same repository and owner-led policy, allocate this issue exactly once, and predate or equal child initialization. Initialization capsule must equal the allocated complete capsule, not merely its IDs. Inherit consumed counts, ancestry, participant classifications and authority history; preserve ancestor outcome and binding records as audit references. Do not inherit readiness, local successful design/challenge/implementation/remediation/review, active/suspended reservations, accepted/verified/reviewed flags or content certificates. Local counts start at zero and gate local prerequisites, including initial_review versus final_review selection. Effective counts alone gate lifetime limits. Missing/cyclic predecessors, wrong prefixes, duplicate allocations and capsule substitutions reject.
invariants.I94AUTH: Audit the complete connected owner-led split component, including descendants and siblings, independent of dictionary traversal, event-file append order or issue number. Normalize user evidence with existing NFKC, whitespace collapse and casefold rules, independently of authority display name. Preserve each original authority occurrence with issue/event origin; inherited copies and exact allocated child-capsule references are references to that occurrence, not new grants. A split authority must be distinct from prior authority identities in its component. Require each allocated child's capsule authorization evidence to normalize to the split authority: this is one split decision referenced by its allocations, never additional grants. An extension, continuation or later split cannot consume any previously used component authority, including sibling capsule or ancestral authority evidence. Preserve the existing explicit policy_transition exception allowing its own initialization authority on that same ticket; do not generalize that exception to siblings or other grant kinds. Capsule updates do not create grants. Detect reuse in either append order, including when a later connection would join formerly separate components. Unconnected historical tickets are not retrospectively treated as one lineage.
invariants.I94IDENTITY: Derive participant history from authoritative events and capsule/owner declarations, including unsuccessful or interrupted phases, original and replacement owners, adoption entries where historically supported, designers, challengers, implementation/remediation/verification authors and initial/final reviewers. Do not infer independence from write_authors alone. Normalize recorded session identity for comparison with NFKC, whitespace collapse and casefold, retaining raw identities and issue/event sources. A child challenge or review cannot use any participant imported from an ancestor. Across different tickets in a connected owner-led split component, a challenge or review identity cannot also be another ticket's declared owner or phase participant; enforce this symmetrically when either history is appended. Existing same-ticket review reuse rules remain unchanged, and all existing same-ticket designer/write-author exclusions remain. Same-role owner reuse across ancestor and child remains permitted for write ownership when it does not conflict with these independent-role rules. Recorded aliases beyond normalization remain a coordinator responsibility. Unknown imported classification fails closed.
invariants.I94ATOMIC: One repository ticket-directory lock acquired before snapshots excludes cooperating append writers, including writes to different issues; lock contention fails closed without publishing. A stale lock is not automatically removed or renewed. Build and validate the complete candidate ledger map, using the exact captured ledger bytes, before temporary-file publication. Immediately before the single os.replace, reread actual event-source bytes when supplied, exact ledger filenames and raw bytes, candidate temp bytes and canonical repository content. Any observed difference or read failure rejects with no candidate ledger replacement. Preserve an external editor's changed bytes rather than restoring them. Cleanup only this operation's owned lock/temp. Canonical content exclusions remain exactly the current ticket ledger and existing ticket-directory lock/temp exclusions. This is observed-input race protection, not an atomic snapshot or lock on arbitrary editors.
invariants.I94HISTORY: Preserve schema 1 and existing event envelope. Dispatch owner-led versus timed split semantics by effective policy. Historical timed replay, budget exhaustion, approved Issue73 bootstrap, prefix rules, original PR/content binding, failed final review stops, and content-bound verification/acceptance/review remain intact. No old certificate certifies a child. Validation of owner-led split components must not reinterpret disconnected timed history or enable a timed predecessor transition.
